title: Anchor induction for marked inverse moments
description: Proves Dirichlet nonvanishing for every positive modulus and character when Re(s) > 2183367/2500000 = 0.8733468, excluding only the principal pole. The actual inverse polynomial and the product of two actual ordinary polynomials, with canonical prime slots (one common relative ray character, bounded heights, possibly overlapping pools), receive row-sized marked-moment estimates on anchor rectangles P <= R, S <= (1-R)/2 + z_R through a simultaneous induction over 176 exactly computed stages. The ordinary half forks the density-split cube-free step with a reference rectangle paid by the parent source after reflection; the inverse half re-runs the canonical-energy initialization with injective marks, selects live slots by the fourth-power Gauss identity, applies a second Poisson summation to one physical row of radius 1-6u, and restores the inverse and slots by reciprocal Euler factors. Children are split into LOW rows (previous anchor after erasing low slots) and HIGH rows (detector counts over sixth-power cofactor cores, with short witnesses paid by earlier anchors and a floored cutoff price), with a principal-character inverse bound for principal rows. The resulting improved inverse and ordinary moments on the line 552429/10^7 - 7227847/10^8 r feed one improved count window of the retuned PR103 return (h = 81447/100000), closed by kernel-checked Bernstein covers, and the Mellin continuation gives the bound. Builds on OpenAI, Hailey Collet, ArviFoxy, Joseph Bebel, Joe Richey, Sil and Jacob Sussman, including the PR93 selected sextic norm, PR97 selected-leaf energy, PR98 physical return, PR103 contact return and PR129 reserve-parametric source lines; inherited notices and licenses are retained. The research and Lean development are AI-assisted.
